root_cause: Off-by-one bound check: the guard `index <= count` accepts index == count, so values[count] (one element past the end of the array) is read. CBMC reports a pointer-outside-object-bounds dereference in values[index] with count == index (e.g. count = 6, index = 6), and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow in the index_equals_count test.
rationale: Valid indices are 0 .. count-1, so the guard must be the strict comparison `index < count`. Every other index (including index == count and SIZE_MAX) falls through to ARRAY_LOOKUP_ERR_RANGE without touching memory or *out. The NULL checks are unchanged.
